name: search-gigs
description: Feature pipeline for the Explore gig search/filter/sort feature: design, implement with tests, independent review loop, and final validation. User story: AS A musician user, I WANT to search for available gigs by text, genre, pay range, and distance from my position, and sort the results, SO THAT I can find and apply for the right gig.

steps.prompt:
You are designing a feature for the Transient app (Expo + React Native + TypeScript, file-based Expo Router, mock-first data). Do NOT edit files; produce a design only.

Feature request from the user: {{task}}

Context you must honor (read these files to confirm before designing):
- Screen to change: src/app/(tabs)/explore.tsx. Today its SearchBar props are hardcoded ("Nashville, TN"), the Filter and Sort chips (local FilterSortChip component) have NO onPress logic, the list shows availableGigs.slice(0,4) with FAKE distance/rating derived from the array index, and no searching/filtering/sorting happens.
- Data: src/data/mockGigs.ts exports MOCK_GIGS (real lat/lng near Nashville) and MOCK_USER_LOCATION. src/data/genres.ts exports ALL_GENRES and GENRE_LABELS. There is NO existing distance/haversine helper anywhere in src/.
- Types: src/types/index.ts (Gig, Genre, GigFilter, MapRegion). Pure service pattern lives in src/data/gigService.ts (pure, immutable, well-tested). Tests use Jest + @testing-library/react-native + fast-check under src/__tests__/.
- Theme/components: src/constants/theme.ts (Brand, Colors, Spacing). Reusable src/components/FilterChip.tsx exists (purple active state). SearchBar at src/components/SearchBar.tsx, GigListingCard at src/components/GigListingCard.tsx accepts a `distance` string prop.

Design scope (keep tight, match existing conventions):
1. A new PURE module src/data/searchService.ts: getDistanceMiles(from,to) via Haversine; a SearchCriteria type { query, genres: Genre[], minPay?, maxPay?, maxDistanceMiles?, sortBy }; sortBy one of 'distance' | 'payHighToLow' | 'payLowToHigh' | 'dateSoonest'; and searchGigs(gigs, userLocation, criteria) that filters by case-insensitive text (title/venue/city), genre overlap, pay range, radius, then sorts. All pure, no mutation.
2. Wire explore.tsx to real state: compute real per-gig distance, feed real distance into GigListingCard, show real result count, remove index-based fakery.
3. A Filter bottom-sheet (genre multi-select reusing FilterChip; pay min/max; distance radius options 5/10/15/25 miles to mirror AMPLIFY_CONFIG.radiusOptions) and a Sort menu (single-select of the four sort options), both wired to the dead chips.
4. Make SearchBar accept a text query and reflect active criteria.

Out of scope: ratings/reviews stay as-is (no rating data in the model); keep the dev loop mock-data driven.

BACKEND ARCHITECTURE (REQUIRED - the project owner is a senior data engineer; new features MUST map cleanly to the Supabase Postgres backend, not just the client). Read src/supabase/schema.sql, src/supabase/types.ts, and BACKEND_SETUP.md first. The gigs table already has title/venue_name/city (text), genres (text[]), pay (integer), latitude/longitude (double precision), but there is NO PostGIS extension, NO spatial column, and NO spatial index (only idx_gigs_hoster_id/status/date), so radius search would be a full-table scan. Your design MUST include:
1. A new idempotent, additive SQL migration under src/supabase/ (e.g. src/supabase/migrations/) that enables PostGIS (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis), adds a geography(Point,4326) location column populated from lat/lng, adds a GIST index on location, and a GIN index on genres for array-overlap filtering, without breaking existing RLS.
2. A Postgres RPC function search_gigs(...) (SECURITY INVOKER so the existing gigs RLS SELECT policy still applies) accepting text query, genres, min/max pay, user lat/lng, radius miles and a sort mode; using ST_DWithin for the radius predicate and ST_Distance for the distance sort; returning gig rows plus a computed distance_miles. Heavy filtering/sorting stays in the database.
3. The TS mapping: searchService.ts calls supabase.rpc search_gigs when a client is configured and falls back to the in-memory pure Haversine filter when supabase is null (mirror the mock-first pattern in src/services/stripeService.ts and src/supabase/client.ts). Define the snake_case row to camelCase domain mapping and update src/supabase/types.ts if a new return shape is needed.
Do NOT run the migration against any real database; it is a committed artifact for the test/prod flow in BACKEND_SETUP.md.

Write the technical design (files to add/change, the exact SearchCriteria/sort contract, the filtering+sorting algorithm, edge cases such as zero-coordinate gigs and empty results, and the test plan listing concrete unit + property tests) to .kiro/workflow-output/search-gigs-design.md. End with send_message severity success and a one-paragraph summary.

Implement the Explore gig search/filter/sort feature for the Transient app according to this design, following the repo's existing conventions (pure service layer + StyleSheet UI + @/ path aliases, default exports for screens).

Design:
{{artifacts.design}}

Aggregated status + review feedback from the previous iteration is in the status file {{artifacts.status}} (its "notes" field; this file does not exist yet on the first pass, so treat a missing file as a fresh start).

Requirements:
- Add src/data/searchService.ts (pure functions only) and its tests under src/__tests__/data/ and/or src/__tests__/properties/ using Jest + fast-check, matching existing test style.
- Update src/app/(tabs)/explore.tsx to use real search/filter/sort state and real distances; remove the index-based fake distance/rating math.
- Add the Filter sheet and Sort menu, wiring the currently dead chips. Reuse src/components/FilterChip.tsx and theme tokens.
- Backend (REQUIRED): add the SQL migration (PostGIS + location geography column + GIST index + genres GIN index) and the search_gigs RPC function under src/supabase/ exactly as the design specifies; update src/supabase/types.ts for any new return shape. searchService.ts must call supabase.rpc when a client exists and fall back to the pure in-memory Haversine filter when supabase is null (mock-first). Do NOT execute the migration against any live database.

After implementing, run: npx tsc --noEmit (the new/changed files must not add type errors) and npx jest for the new/affected tests. Then write .kiro/workflow-output/search-gigs-status.json with fields: { "complete": false, "iteration": <n>, "typecheckClean": <bool for the feature files>, "testsPassing": <bool>, "filesChanged": [paths], "notes": "..." }. Set complete only in the aggregate step, not here. Finish with send_message severity success summarizing what you built and the test results.

branches.prompt: Independently review ONLY the search/filter/sort implementation just made (src/data/searchService.ts and src/app/(tabs)/explore.tsx). Focus on logic correctness: Haversine distance accuracy and units (miles), case-insensitive text matching across title/venue/city, genre overlap semantics, inclusive/exclusive pay-range bounds, radius filtering, sort stability and correctness for all four sort modes, and handling of zero/invalid coordinates and empty-result states. Verify functions are pure (no mutation of inputs). Report concrete findings as PASS or a specific list of required changes. Be precise about file and line.

Independently review ONLY the tests and UI wiring for the search/filter/sort feature. Check: tests actually cover filtering by text/genre/pay/distance and all sort modes plus edge cases (empty query, no matches, zero-coordinate gig); tests follow the repo's Jest + fast-check conventions; the Filter sheet and Sort menu are wired to real state and update the result count; SearchBar reflects the active query; the index-based fake distance/rating math has been removed; accessibility labels/roles are present on new interactive elements. Report PASS or a specific list of required changes with file and line.

steps.prompt:
Final validation gate for the Explore search/filter/sort feature. Do not add new features. Run, in the repo root:
1. npx tsc --noEmit  (confirm the feature files src/data/searchService.ts and src/app/(tabs)/explore.tsx introduce no new type errors; note any pre-existing unrelated errors separately).
2. npx jest for the search feature test files.
3. npx expo export --platform web --output-dir /tmp/search-gigs-verify  (confirm the app still bundles).

Then write a concise go/no-go report to .kiro/workflow-output/search-gigs-validation.md covering: the user story acceptance (search by text, genre, pay, distance; sort works; results + count update), command results, files changed, and anything still open. Finish with send_message severity success if the feature meets the user story and the app bundles, otherwise severity error with the blocking reasons.
